en: The Apadāna of the Elder Nuns,
Chapter on the Khattiyas,
2: The Apadāna of the Eighty-four Thousand Bhikkhunīs.
“Eighty-four thousand [people],
born into brahmin families,
with delicate hands and feet,”
They belong purely to you, O Great Sage.
Gods, nāgas, and kinnaras, born into the clans of vessas and suddas, [all honor you].
O Great Sage, in your city there were many maidens from the four continents;
some among them have gone forth into the religious life.
Many who see all things—
devas, kinnaras, and nāgas—
will touch it in the future.
Having experienced all glory and attained every perfection,
they have gained confidence in you.
They will awaken in the future. We,
however, are daughters of brahmins,
born into a family of brahmins.
Beholding you, O Great Hero,
we worship your feet, O Seer;
all our existences have been brought to an end.
Root craving has been uprooted;
the underlying tendencies have been severed,
and the formations of merit have been shattered.
All spheres of concentration have been mastered through the power of meditative attainments;
by means of jhāna, one finds delight in the Dhamma.
We shall dwell forever [in peace].
The conduit to existence and ignorance,
as well as the volitional formations, have been exhausted.
“Having reached the state so very difficult to see, grant us leave, O Leader! You have been our benefactors.
“You have been helpful to me,” [said the Buddha].
Those who have practiced for a long time—
having cut through the four doubts,
may they all go to Nibbāna.”
Having paid homage at the feet of the Sage and performed a display of supernormal power,
some women manifested light.
Then others show darkness, as well as the moon and the sun,
and the ocean filled with fish.
They show Mount Sineru and its surrounding terraces,
as well as the Pāricchattaka tree and the abode of the Thirty-three gods.
They display the Yāma heaven through their supernormal power,
as well as the Tusita heaven, the Nimmānarati gods,
and the Vasavatti Mahissara gods.
Some Brahmās showed themselves,
as well as a magnificent cloister;
having fashioned the form of Brahmā, they appeared.
They teach the Dhamma of emptiness.
Having performed various transformations and displayed psychic power to the Teacher, they said:
All the women displayed their strength and paid homage at the feet of the Teacher:
"May we be masters of the supernormal powers (iddhi),..."
With the divine ear-element and the knowledge of penetrating others' minds,
we have attained mastery, O Great Sage.
We know our former abodes,
the divine eye is purified,
and all taints are utterly exhausted.
Now there is no further becoming.
Regarding the meaning, the Dhamma, etymological definitions,
and likewise inspired eloquence;
O Great Hero, knowledge has arisen within us in your presence.
[We have seen] the former Protectors of the World.
Our meeting has been shown to you;
we have performed much service for your sake, O Great Sage.
O Sage, remember that wholesome deed which we have performed for your sake, O Great Hero.
We have not accumulated merit.
One hundred thousand aeons ago,
there was the Great Sage Padumuttara.
There was a city named Haṃsavatī,
the ancestral home of the Perfectly Enlightened One.
By means of the gate of Haṃsavatī—
The Ganges flows at all times;
pressed back by the river, those monks cannot proceed.
For one day, for two or three days,
for seven days, for a month,
and then for a full four-month period;
They could not proceed. At that time,
there was a royal chaplain named Jaṭila, who was the essence among beings.
Seeing the river Ganges obstructed, O monks,
he had a bridge constructed;
at that time, by means of hundreds of thousands [of workers].
He caused a bridge to be built over the Ganges and had a monastery constructed on the near bank for the Sangha.
Women and men alike,
high and low families as well,
his bridge and his monastery—
They made it equal for us and for other human beings with a mind of complete clarity.
Among the teachings, they are his heirs—
in the cities and in the provinces—
whether women, men, or boys.
And many young girls scattered sand over the Setu monastery.
Having swept the path, [set up] plantain trees,
full jars, and banners;
[and offer] incense, powder, and garlands.
Having performed service for the Teacher and having had a monastery built at Setuvihāra,
he invited the Guide.
Having given a great gift,
I aspired for supreme enlightenment.
Padumuttara, the Great Hero—
The Great Sage, the deliverer of all living beings, performed an act worthy of appreciation for the matted-hair ascetic.
"When a hundred thousand eons have passed,
there will be a fortunate aeon;
having experienced existence after existence,"
They shall attain enlightenment.
Men and women who have performed service with their own hands— having been skilled in such service— shall reach that state.
"In a future time,
they will all be present before me.
By the ripening of that karma,
And through their volitions and aspirations,
they have been born in the celestial realm as your attendants.
We shall serve you with divine pleasures beyond counting,
and with human pleasures beyond counting.
We have wandered through existence after existence.
A hundred thousand aeons ago,
we performed a perfection of well-done deeds.
Among humans and likewise in the excellent city of the gods,
he was exceedingly delicate in form, enjoyments, and glory.
Furthermore, we always obtain fame and honor,
as well as every success resulting from well-performed deeds.
Having reached our final existence,
we were born into a brahmin family;
our hands and feet are delicate and smooth.
In the dwelling of the Sakyan son,
we do not see the earth adorned at any time whatsoever.
O Great Sage, we do not see any muddy ground or impurity while we dwell in our homes.
They always bring all kinds of honor at all times;
this is due to the fruit of their past karma.
Having abandoned the household life and gone forth into homelessness,
they have crossed over the path of saṃsāra.
We have become free from passion.
Robes, almsfood,
requisites, and lodgings—
"Thousands [of defilements] bring us from here and there;
our defilements have been incinerated."
we dwell free from taints.
Welcome indeed has come to us!
the Buddha’s teaching has been accomplished.
The four analytical knowledges (paṭisambhidā) have been attained.
the Buddha's teaching has been accomplished.
Thus indeed, eighty-four thousand brahmin maidens who had become bhikkhunīs recited these verses in the presence of the Blessed One.
The second account: the legend of the eighty-four thousand bhikkhunīs.
